properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Kept as an idea by @ajs, 2026-10-22.

FROM Tao (same page): his "Math 2.0" work includes "ablation studies" and "exploring neighborhoods of theorems", and "finding new principles and methods rather than proofs".

TODAY, by hand: every trial ran propagate_from one premise at a time.
- Heat rung: Leibniz → the energy line falls, the theorem stands on the max-principle line; k > 0 → both fall until Proposition F; and so on.
- Lucas–Penrose: "we know our own consistency" → the main line falls, the rival is untouched; Gödel I → both fall.
That IS an ablation, done one call at a time.

The existing open idea dec:idea-reflow2-computes-a-conclusions-minimal-cut-sets-of-premises asks for the set-wise version: which sets of premises, rejected together, sink a conclusion.

OPTIONS:
(a) one call that ablates every foundation of a conclusion singly and tabulates it (premise → falls / stands, and via which route);
(b) the minimal cut sets (the existing idea), with (a) as its first rung;
(c) nothing new; the agent loops propagate_from.

PUSHBACK: a whole-design ablation is expensive (one walk per foundation; the heat design has about 20), and its reply must stay inside the budget (today's size findings). The single-premise table is the useful 80%.

SIZE (a finding): (a) moderate; (b) larger; (c) nothing.
